alternatives.argument: The carrier directly defines the finite periodic, infinite, and Dirichlet index sets, weighted norms, and difference operators needed below; these are definitions, not an unproved theorem.

The carrier states all five periodic/infinite stencils explicitly and separately specifies the positive-speed finite-interval upwind initial and inflow rows; no stability conclusion is built into the definition.
The carrier defines the real centered two-step recurrence, periodic and homogeneous-Dirichlet rows, and start data as displacement plus discrete initial velocity V^0, with U^1=U^0+kV^0.

For d_j=v_j-v_{j-1}, expand the complex interior sum as -h^{-1}Σu_j overline(d_{j+1}-d_j), shift indices, and collect the edge inner product plus conjugated endpoint terms u_0 overline(d_1)/h-u_N overline(d_N)/h.
Write w_j=Σ_{i<j}d_i with d_i=w_{i+1}-w_i; expand jΣ|d_i|²-|Σd_i|²=Σ_{i<r}|d_i-d_r|². This yields |w_j|²≤NΣ_{i=0}^{N-1}|d_i|²; summing and using L=Nh gives ||w||_h²≤L²||D_+w||_{e,h}².

For a<0, reflect x and the stencil to reduce to positive speed. Differentiate u_t=-a u_x, use the C^6 mixed-partial symmetry supplier to obtain u_tt=a^2u_xx and u_ttt=-a^3u_xxx, and Taylor-expand time and space lines. The Lax–Friedrichs h^2/k term is O(h) under the lower k/h bound; the Lax–Wendroff second-order time term cancels.

The cross-gradient product equals ||D_+bar U||²-(k²/4)||D_+V||². The finite edge estimate ||D_+V||²≤4h^{-2}||V||² gives the stated (1-ν²) coefficient. Multiplying the recurrence by the centered time difference and applying the local summation-by-parts identity shows conservation.

Substitute z^j into each of the five updates, use z^{-1}=bar z and |z|=1, and multiply each factor by its conjugate to obtain the five displayed squared-modulus formulas. The batch-37 periodic heat lemma supplies the finite orthogonal Fourier basis.

Use the batch-37 periodic second-difference eigenvalue λ_ℓ=4h^{-2}s_ℓ to derive the scalar recurrence. Classify its characteristic roots; for ν≤ν₀<1 solve nonzero modes and bound the geometric quotient, and at ν=1 solve the even-grid Nyquist double root explicitly.

Classify the squared moduli by the signs of ν(1-ν), 1-ν², and S²; a nonconstant Fourier mode provides each stated instability. Orthogonal diagonalization converts symbol bounds to exact operator-power bounds.

Construct the fixed smooth datum by scaling the published compact cutoff and choose the target grid node with the published floor lemma; prove the nearest-neighbor dependence cone by induction and compute the constant-speed characteristic. For the separate sufficiency warning, use N_q=4q, fixed period P, h_q=P/N_q, k_q=h_q/(2a), and the mode ℓ=q with z=i; its centered multiplier has modulus sqrt(5)/2, so at floor(T/k_q) the grid operator powers have no uniform finite-time bound.
